transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah… I’m here because I guess I’ve just stopped caring about things. Stuff I used to look forward to, you know? My fishing gear’s been sitting in the garage untouched, and normally I’d be out checking the rods or planning a weekend, but now I just walk past it.

Even the woodshop—I've got projects half-started, and I used to love that. Now it feels like another chore, like paperwork at a job site. And my kids will ask me to play chess, and I’ll sit there, but I’m not really in it. I’m just kind of moving pieces around.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It’s been… about a year and seven months, I think. It kind of started after my wife’s health problems changed everything at home. Time’s gotten weird since then—I measure it by doctor visits and things around the house more than months, but yeah, roughly that long.
Have you noticed that you no longer get pleasure or satisfaction from activities that you used to enjoy?

Yeah… that’s pretty much it. I mean, I used to really look forward to fishing—checking the rods, getting the tackle sorted, all that—and now the gear’s just sitting in the garage like it belongs to somebody else.

Same with the woodshop. I’ll walk in there and see stuff half-started, and instead of wanting to finish it, it just feels like another job I don’t have the energy to deal with. Even chess with my kids… I’ll sit down because they ask me to, but I’m not really enjoying it. I’m just moving the pieces around, waiting for it to be over, I guess.
Do you find yourself feeling down or low most of the time these days?

I don’t know… “down” is hard to pin down. Some days I’d call it that, I guess, but it’s not like I’m walking around crying all the time or anything. It’s more like everything’s got this gray layer over it.

Like, I’ll be driving past a job site and start thinking about the schedule, concrete delivery, whether the crew remembered to cover things if it rains—and then I realize I’m not even really thinking about work, I’m just kind of staring through it. So… yeah, maybe low. But I don’t always know what to call it.
Have you been feeling tired or lacking energy a lot of the time, even when you haven’t been doing much?

Yeah… a lot. It’s strange because I’m not even doing the hardest stuff most of the time—I’m managing it, checking on things, walking the project—but by midmorning I feel like I’ve already put in a full shift.

And stairs, even just going up with the crew to look at something, it feels like… I don’t know, like my body’s dragging wet concrete around. Which is stupid to say, given the job, but that’s what it feels like. I used to move around sites all day without thinking about it, and now I’m looking for excuses to stay put.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, feeling restless or unable to sit still more often than not?

I don’t know… I haven’t really noticed that, not in a clear way. I mean, my wife might say I take longer to answer sometimes, but she also says I’ve always done that when I’m thinking, so who knows.

At work, sometimes the guys are talking and I realize I’m a step behind, but that might just be me being distracted. And restless… I don’t think so. I’ll sit there, but then I start thinking about whether I ordered the right lumber package or if the inspector’s going to make a fuss about something dumb, and—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

So… no, I’m not sure I’ve noticed moving or talking slower, and I wouldn’t say I’m pacing around or anything.
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or blaming yourself for things more often than not, even when it’s not entirely your fault?

Yeah… yeah, I do. Probably more than I should.

It’s like, if something goes sideways, I don’t just think, “Okay, that was a mistake.” I go straight to, “Of course, because I’m the one in charge and I’m useless.” Like if we miss an appointment, or the numbers come in over what I said, or there’s some safety thing the guys bring up—even if it’s something that could’ve happened to anyone—I take it like it proves something about me.

And it’s not just work. I’ll be sitting at home and thinking I’ve let my wife down, the kids too. Then I start thinking the guys on the site would be better off if someone else was running things. I mean, I know construction always has problems—weather, suppliers, inspectors, all that—but somehow it still feels like it lands on me. Like I should’ve prevented it, and if I didn’t, then what good am I?
Have you completely lost interest in any activities, to the point where you don’t even feel like trying them anymore, not even a little?

Yeah… I think that’s probably true. I mean, “completely” sounds strong, but… I don’t really try anymore.

Like my fishing stuff is still sitting in the garage. Rods, tackle boxes, all of it. I used to mess with that stuff even if I wasn’t going out—clean things up, check lures, whatever. Now I walk past it and it’s like it belongs to somebody else.

Same with the woodshop. I used to like making little things, fixing up stuff around the house, but now it feels like another job I don’t want to start. And the kids will ask me to play chess sometimes, and I’ll sit down because I don’t want to be a jerk, but I’m not really there. I’m just moving pieces around, waiting for it to be over, which… sounds awful when I say it out loud.

Sorry, I’m getting off track. But yeah, I’ve stopped caring about most of the things I used to actually look forward to.
